groups.question: what persisted state does it touch, and does it change only as the binding says?
groups.title: State

groups.question: does any answer depend on more than recorded state and arguments?
groups.title: Transformation

groups.question: which one kind of effect does it do, and where does each failure go?
groups.title: Effect

groups.question: which document gives it its meaning?
groups.title: Semantics

groups.question: does a conclusion depend on absence? Is its scope closed? Could more input withdraw it?
groups.title: CALM

questions.question: Where does the state this change touches live?
questions.reason: Every place it lives is a place it can be wrong and a place a reader must look.

questions.question: Which functions this change adds or edits are pure, their answer depending on their arguments alone?
questions.reason: Pure functions can be tested without the world and reasoned about locally.

questions.question: Which line is the first that changes anything a caller can see afterwards: an argument it passed, a global, a file, a socket, a process?
questions.reason: Everything before it can be retried and tested without the world; after it, something has happened.

questions.question: What is verified before the first effect runs: parses, assertions, permission checks?
questions.reason: A check after the effect cannot prevent it.

questions.question: What can happen after this change that could not before: which inputs behave differently, what can a caller or reader now observe?
questions.reason: A change is judged by what it makes possible, and every other answer here can hold while this one is wrong.
questions.where: at the line that makes it possible

questions.question: Where is a failure after the first effect recorded or handled?
Where does the code take authority from its surroundings (a fixed path, an environment variable, the current directory, a global) instead of from what it was given?
questions.reason: Each such place is one the caller cannot confine.

questions.question: Which conclusions depend on the input being complete or on something being absent, and where does the code wait for that?
questions.reason: A conclusion drawn early can be withdrawn by more input.
questions.where: at the wait or the closed scope

questions.question: Which decisions or specification sections give this change its meaning?
Which test or check would fail if this change were wrong?
Which planted fault shows that the check can fail?
questions.reason: A check that has never failed proves nothing.
